visuals.classification_reason: Required to evaluate this specific evidence: A shift in both dimensions partitions an 8×8 block into four parts; zero shift along one dimension reduces this to two, and fully aligned grids to one. Regions in the same relative position across blocks share a structural compression pattern, although their actual image content and quantization errors differ. The method exploits that structural similarity rather than asserting identical errors.

visuals.review_notes: Directly inspected complete PDF page render; captions and numbers cross-checked with PDF text. Full-page asset selected to prevent heuristic clipping.
visuals.classification_reason: Required to evaluate this specific evidence: The predictor uses only the upper-left 44×44 patch and a lightweight ResNet-18-derived network with depthwise-separable convolutions. Six hybrid blocks form the reconstructor; each combines four standard and two pattern-clustered layers. The predicted offset controls rearrangement, while learned attention estimates useful content. Predictor pretraining followed by freezing avoids conflating offset learning with the reconstruction stage.

visuals.label: Figure 3
visuals.caption: The demonstration of pattern clustering module.
visuals.raw_text: Fig. 3: The demonstration of pattern clustering module.
visuals.review_notes: Directly inspected complete PDF page render; captions and numbers cross-checked with PDF text. Full-page asset selected to prevent heuristic clipping.
visuals.classification_reason: Required to evaluate this specific evidence: For a teaching example with a 4-row, 2-column partition, an 8×8 block divides into areas 8, 24, 8 and 24 pixels. Matching parts from many blocks are packed into four feature groups; attention mixes tokens within the regrouped windows, then inverse clustering restores coordinates. A wrong phase still changes spatial reach but no longer guarantees matching compression patterns. Grouping is a permutation, not a loss of pixels, and does not make attention global over the entire image.

Against SwinIR, the paper reports about +0.06 dB; for LIVE1 (30,50,4,4), 32.77→32.86 dB. OAPT is not best in every row: Classic5 (50,30,4,4) gives 32.97 versus ART’s 33.02. L1 offset regression encourages central values when evidence is ambiguous. Exact classification accuracy and restoration quality need not move together, because even an incorrect permutation may enlarge spatial access. Table 4 quantifies that distinction.

visuals.classification_reason: Required to evaluate this specific evidence: At (10,90,0,2), accuracy is 97% and both score 29.77 dB. At (90,10,2,0), accuracy is 0%, yet OAPT gives 29.57 versus SwinIR 29.54 and oracle 29.62. Thus restoration gains can survive incorrect phase estimates, while true phase still helps. The most important limitation is unreliable offset identification, not an absolute inability to handle repeated JPEG.
